rule: Default NOT_COMPARABLE. A cell is CONDITIONALLY_COMPARABLE only if every generic check, every allow-listed definition, every policy requirement and every metric condition passes, every used item is a finite number with its declared definition, no item of an inapplicable reclassification path or forbidden item is supplied, and all guards hold. Nothing is defaulted. Display is BLOCKED for every cell in B06.
check_order: input shape (example, meta, items, policy, meta.period, meta.fx, meta.item_definitions)
period (kind, real dates, order, duration, stand-alone quarter, TTM components, balance dates)
currency and FX (supported currency, no FX for USD, rate > 0, source, basis per measure, average window = period / closing date = period end)
computation with every intermediate value finite
pair_rule: Two cells compare only if both pass, period kind/start/end are equal, the recipe's homogeneity fields are equal and the policy objects are equal.

recipes.name: EBIT and EBITDA, normalised

definition.numerator: Operating profit before finance costs and tax, excluding impairments and reversals, downstream inventory at replacement cost (IFRS) or LIFO (US GAAP), leases aligned to IFRS 16; EBITDA adds DD&A

ordered_steps: Validate generic fields and definitions.
Start from operating profit as defined (before finance costs and tax).
Add impairment losses; subtract reversals (IFRS only).
IFRS: subtract the disclosed inventory holding gain; US GAAP LIFO: subtract any LIFO liquidation gain.
US GAAP EBIT: add the disclosed interest-equivalent part of operating lease cost; EBITDA: add DD&A and the full operating lease cost.
Items that belong to another basis are rejected, not ignored.
Convert at the period-average rate.
recipes.ifrs_vs_us_gaap: IAS 36 reversal vs none under US GAAP; IAS 2 bans LIFO; IFRS 16 vs ASC 842 operating lease cost; IFRS 6 vs successful efforts/full cost.

recipes.name: Operating cash flow: reported, and after lease payments (derived research measure)

definition.numerator: reported_cfo = published CFO. cfo_after_lease_payments = published CFO, minus lease principal (and interest) published in financing, plus dividends received published in investing, plus dividends paid published in operating

ordered_steps: Validate generic fields; classifications of interest, dividends and every lease cash flow must be recorded, in their allow-lists and consistent with the framework.
reported_cfo: the published figure, converted only.
cfo_after_lease_payments, IFRS: subtract lease principal (financing); if interest paid (incl. lease interest) sits in financing, subtract it; lease interest must sit with other interest paid.
cfo_after_lease_payments, US GAAP: operating-lease payments and finance-lease interest are already in operating; subtract finance-lease principal (financing).
If dividends received sit in investing (IFRS), add the disclosed amount; if dividends paid sit in operating (IFRS), add them back.
A move item supplied when the published classification does not require it, or an unrecognised item, rejects the cell (no double deduction).
Interest received outside operating -> NOT_COMPARABLE (no recipe).
Convert at the period-average rate.
recipes.ifrs_vs_us_gaap: IAS 7 classification choices vs ASC 230; IFRS 16 (principal financing) vs ASC 842 (operating lease payments operating, finance lease principal financing).

handling.restatements: Only the latest restated comparative (restated_latest = true); the filing vintage is recorded.
handling.definition_conflict: Every required definition is an allow-list; a missing or unlisted value -> NOT_COMPARABLE with the field name.

failure_conditions.reason: US GAAP classifies interest paid in operating activities.
US GAAP classifies dividends paid in financing activities.
US GAAP investing distributions are returns of investment, not dividends from earnings; no reconciliation recipe.
interest_paid_in_financing is defined to include lease interest; a split placement has no recipe.

recipes.notes: reported_cfo is the published IFRS/US GAAP figure, converted only; it is not comparable across frameworks and FCF never uses it. cfo_after_lease_payments is a derived research measure, not the published accounting CFO: operating cash flow with ALL lease payments (principal and interest) and all interest paid deducted, dividends received from investments included, dividends paid (parent and NCI) excluded. This target matches what ASC 842 operating-lease reporters already publish, so IFRS 16 and US GAAP finance-lease principal is moved in from financing; each cash flow is deducted exactly once (the published classification decides whether a move is needed; a move item supplied when the classification does not require it is rejected). Basis: IAS 7 permits operating or financing for interest paid and dividends paid, operating or investing for dividends received; IFRS 16 places lease principal in financing; ASC 842 places operating-lease payments and finance-lease interest in operating and finance-lease principal in financing (standards text not opened in this environment: UNVERIFIED reference). Disclosures used: the cash-flow statement lines named in item_definitions.

recipes.name: Capital expenditure, cash basis

definition.numerator: Cash payments for PP&E and capitalised exploration/intangibles; acquisitions of businesses and investments in associates/JVs excluded

ordered_steps: Validate generic fields.

Full-cost reporters are not accepted.
The capex lines must exclude lease payments and non-cash right-of-use additions (leases are deducted once, in M05).
Capex = PP&E payments + exploration/intangible payments.
Convert at the period-average rate.

recipes.name: Net debt and gearing

definition.numerator: Net debt = borrowings + all lease liabilities - cash and cash equivalents
definition.denominator: Gearing = net debt / (net debt + total equity incl. NCI)

ordered_steps: Validate generic fields; the balance date is the period end.
Cash definition must be cash and cash equivalents only.
Hybrids: has_hybrids must be stated; when true, hybrids must be inside borrowings.
Include all lease liabilities on both frameworks.
Gearing denominator must be positive.
Convert balances at the closing rate dated the period end.
